questions.q: In a double slit experiment shown in figure, when light of wavelength $400$ nm is used, dark fringe is observed at $P$. If $D = 0 . 2m$, the minimum distance between the slits ${S}_{1}$ and ${S}_{2}$ is $\alphamm$. Write the value of $10\alpha$ to the nearest integer.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
According to the given diagram, the path difference for minima at P is given by

$∆ x = 2\sqrt{D^{2} + d^{2}} - 2D . . . \left(1\right)$

And, from the condition of minima, it follows that

$∆ x = $\dfrac{λ}{2} . . . \left(2\right)$

Equations (1) and (2) imply that

2\sqrt{D^{2} + d^{2}} -$2D = $\dfrac{λ}{2}

$⇒ $\sqrt{D^{2} + d^{2}} -$D = $\dfrac{λ}{4}

$⇒ $\sqrt{D^{2} + d^{2}} = \dfrac{λ}{4} +$D$

$⇒ D^{2} + d^{2} = D^{2} + $\dfrac{\lambda2}{16} + \dfrac{D\lambda}{2}

$⇒ d^{2} = $\dfrac{D\lambda}{2} + \dfrac{\lambda2}{16}

$⇒ d^{2} = $\dfrac{0 . 2 \times 400 \times {10}^{- 9}}{2} + \dfrac{16 \times {10}^{- 14}}{16}

$⇒ d^{2} \approx 400 \times {10}^{- 10}$

$\begin{cases}∴ d & = & 20 \times {10}^{- 5}m \\ & = & 0 . 20mm\end{cases}$$

Therefore, $10\alpha = 2$.

questions.q: Sodium light of wavelengths $650$ nm and $655$ nm is used to study diffraction at a single slit of aperture $0 . 5mm$. The distance between the slit and the screen is $2 . 0m$. The separation between the positions of the first maxima of diffraction pattern obtained in the two cases is _____~$\times {10}^{- 5}m$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The condition for maxima in diffraction is,

$bsin\theta = \left(2n + 1\right)\dfrac{λ}{2}$.

~For the first maxima~$n = 1$. Therefore,

$bsin\theta = \dfrac{3\lambda}{2} ⇒ sin\theta = \dfrac{3\lambda}{2b} = \dfrac{y}{D}y = \dfrac{3\lambdaD}{2b}$

Now the difference between the positions of the maxima will be,

${y}_{1} - {y}_{2} = \dfrac{3D}{2b}\left({λ}_{1} - {λ}_{2}\right) ⇒ {y}_{1} - {y}_{2} = \dfrac{3 \times 2}{2 \times 5 \times {10}^{- 4}} \times \left(655 - 650\right) \times {10}^{- 9} = 3 \times {10}^{- 5}m$

questions.q: A source of light is placed in front of a screen. The intensity of light on the screen is $I$. Two Polaroids ${P}_{1}$ and ${P}_{2}$ are so placed in between the source of light and screen that the intensity of light on the screen is $\dfrac{I}{2}$.~Then the ${P}_{2}$,~should be rotated by an angle of (degrees) so that the intensity of light on the screen becomes~$\dfrac{3I}{8}$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Recall the law of Malus& $I^{'} = \dfrac{I}{2}\cos^{2}\theta$

Here~$\theta$~is the angle between two polaroids,~

$⇒ \dfrac{3I}{8} = \dfrac{I}{2}\cos^{2}\theta⇒ \theta = 30 °$.

questions.q:
In Young’s double slit experiment, two slits ${S}_{1}$~and ${S}_{2}$ are $d$~distance apart and the separation from slits to screen is $D$ (as shown in figure). Now if two transparent slabs of equal thickness $0 . 1mm$ but refractive index $1 . 51$ and $1 . 55$ are introduced in the path of beam \left(\lambda = 4000Å\right)$~from ${S}_{1}$ and ${S}_{2}$ respectively. The central bright fringe spot will shift by ________ number of fringes.

$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The change in path difference due to the two slabs at $P$ is~$\Deltax = \left({μ}_{2} - {μ}_{1}\right)t$

$= ( 1 . 55 - 1 . 51 ) \times 0 . 1= 0 . 04 \times {10}^{- 4}$

$⇒ \Deltax = 4 \times {10}^{- 6} = 4\mu m$

Now, the~distance of central maxima from geometrical center is~$y = \dfrac{\DeltaxD}{d} = 4 \times {10}^{- 6}\dfrac{D}{d}$

Now, fringe width,~$n\beta = 4 \times {10}^{- 6}\dfrac{D}{d}$

Or,~$\dfrac{n\lambdaD}{d} = 4 \times {10}^{- 6}\dfrac{D}{d}$

Number of shift,~$n = \dfrac{4 \times {10}^{- 6}}{4 \times {10}^{- 7}} = 10$.

questions.q: In a single slit diffraction pattern, a light of wavelength $6000\overset{o}{A}$ is used. The distance between the first and third minima in the diffraction pattern is found to be $3$ mm when the screen is placed $50$ cm away from slits. The width of the slit is ____\times {10}^{- 4}m.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For $n^{th}$ minima:

$⇒ bsin\theta = n\lambda$

($\lambda$ is very small, so $sin\theta$ is very small, hence $sin\theta ≃ tan\theta$.

$⇒ btan\theta = n\lambda$

$⇒ b\dfrac{y}{D} = n\lambda$

$⇒ {y}_{n} = \dfrac{n\lambdaD}{b}$ (Position of $n^{th}$ minima)

$B \to {1}^{st}$ minima and $A \to {3}^{rd}$:

${y}_{3} = \dfrac{3\lambdaD}{b}, {y}_{1} = \dfrac{\lambdaD}{b}$

$⇒ \Deltay = {y}_{3} - {y}_{1} = \dfrac{2\lambdaD}{b}$

$⇒ 3 \times {10}^{- 3} = \dfrac{2 \times 6000 \times {10}^{- 10} \times 0 . 5}{b}$

$⇒ b = \dfrac{2 \times 6000 \times {10}^{- 10} \times 0 . 5}{3 \times {10}^{- 3}}$

$⇒ b = 2 \times {10}^{- 4}m$

questions.q: An unpolarized light beam is incident on the polarizer of a polarization experiment and the intensity of light beam emerging from the analyzer is measured as $100$ Lumens. Now, if the analyzer is rotated around the horizontal axis (direction of light) by $30 °$ in clockwise direction, the intensity of emerging light will be _______Lumens.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Assuming initially axis of Polarizer and Analyzer are parallel

Now emerging intensity $= \dfrac{I0}{2}\cos^{2}30 °$

$= 100\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right)2 = 100 \times \dfrac{3}{4} = 75$

questions.q: A Young's double-slit experiment is performed using monochromatic light of wavelength& $\lambda$. The intensity of light at a point on the screen, where the path difference is~$\lambda$, is~$K$~units. The intensity of light at a point where the path difference is~$\dfrac{λ}{6}$~is given by~$\dfrac{nK}{12}$, where~$n$~is an integer. The value of~$n$& is&
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$I = {I}_{0}\cos^{2}\dfrac{ϕ}{2}$

$= {kcos}^{2} \left(\dfrac{π}{λ} \times \dfrac{λ}{6}\right)$

$= k\cos^{2} \left(\dfrac{π}{6})$

$= \dfrac{3k}{4} = \dfrac{9k}{12}$

$n = 9

$

questions.q: A parallel beam of monochromatic light of wavelength $5000\overset{o}{A}$ is incident normally on a single narrow slit of width $0 . 001mm$. The light is focused by convex lens on screen, placed on its focal plane. The first minima will be formed for the angle of diffraction of ______ (degree).
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The condition for the first minima in the single slit diffraction experiment can be written as

$asin\theta = \lambda . . . \left(1\right)$

Equation (1) implies that

$sin\theta = $\dfrac{λ}{a} = \dfrac{5000 \times {10}^{- 10}}{1 \times {10}^{- 6}} = \dfrac{1}{2}

$⇒ \theta =30 °

$

questions.q: In a Young's double slit experiment $15$ fringes are observed on a small portion of the screen when light of wavelength $500$ nm is used. Ten fringes are observed on the same section of the screen when another light source of wavelength $\lambda$ is used. Then the value of $\lambda$ is (in $nm$ ) __________.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$15 \times 500 \times \dfrac{D}{d} = 10 \times {\lambda}_{2} \times \dfrac{D}{d}$
${λ}_{2} = 15 \times 50nm$
${λ}_{2} = 750nm$

questions.subject: Physics

questions.q: Two wavelengths $\lambda_1$ and $\lambda_2$ are used in Young's double slit experiment. $\lambda_1=450 \mathrm{~nm}$ and $\lambda_2=650 \mathrm{~nm}$. The minimum order of fringe produced by $\lambda_2$ which overlaps with the fringe produced by $\lambda_1$ is $n$. The value of $n$ is _____.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{n}_2 \lambda_2=\mathrm{n}_1 \lambda_1 \\ & \frac{\mathrm{n}_2}{\mathrm{n}_1}=\frac{\lambda_1}{\lambda_2}=\frac{450}{650}=\frac{9}{13} \\ & \mathrm{n}_2=9\end{aligned}$

questions.q: In a Young's double slit experiment, two slits are located 1.5 mm apart. The distance of screen from slits is 2 m and the wavelength of the source is 400 nm. If the 20 maxima of the double slit pattern are contained within the centre maximum of the single slit diffraction pattern, then the width of each slit is $\mathrm{x} \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~cm}$, where x -value is ________
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Width of 20 maxima of double slit = width of central maxima of single slit
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{20 \lambda \mathrm{D}}{\mathrm{~d}}=\frac{2 \lambda \mathrm{D}}{\mathrm{a}} \\ & \frac{10}{\mathrm{~d}}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{a}} \\ & \mathrm{a}=\frac{\mathrm{d}}{10}=\frac{1.5 \times 10^{-1}}{10} \mathrm{~cm}=15 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~cm}
\end{aligned}$
Value of $x$ is 15
Answer is 15

questions.q: As shown in the figure, in Young's double slit experiment, a thin plate of thickness $t = 10\mu m$~and refractive index $\mu = 1 . 2$~is inserted infront of slit ${S}_{1}$. The experiment is conducted in air ($\mu = 1$) and uses a monochromatic light of wavelength $\lambda = 500nm$. Due to the insertion of the plate, central maxima is shifted by a distance of $x{β}_{0}$.~${β}_{0}$ is the fringe-width before the insertion of the plate. The value of the $x$ is ______.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Fringe shift due to slab& in Young's double slit experiment is given by& $∆ x = \dfrac{D ( \mu - 1 ) t}{d}$

Since, fringe width~${β}_{0} = \dfrac{D}{d}\lambda$

Then,~$∆ x = \dfrac{{β}_{0}\left(\mu - 1\right)t}{λ}$

Putting the values, we have

$= \dfrac{10 \times {10}^{- 6} ( 1 . 2 - 1 )}{5 \times {10}^{- 7}}{β}_{0}$

$= \dfrac{{10}^{- 5} \times 0 . 2}{5 \times {10}^{- 7}}{β}_{0} = 4{β}_{0}$

Hence, the value of~$x = 4$.

questions.q: In a Young’s double slit experiment, the intensities at two points, for the path difference& $\dfrac{λ}{4}$~and~$\dfrac{λ}{3}$~($\lambda$~being the wavelength of light used) are ${I}_{1}$ and ${I}_{2}$ respectively. If ${I}_{0}$ denotes the intensity produced by each one of the individual slits, then~\dfrac{{I}_{1} + {I}_{2}}{I0} = ______.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As we know, resultant intensity is given by,

$I = 4{I}_{0}\cos^{2} \left(\dfrac{\Deltaϕ}{2}\right)~and phase difference can be written as~$∆ ϕ = $\dfrac{2\pi}{λ}$∆ x$.

For first case:

${I}_{1} = 4{I}_{0}\cos^{2}\left(\dfrac{2\pi}{λ} \times \dfrac{λ}{4}\right) =$4{I}_{0}\cos^{2}\left(\dfrac{π}{4}\right) =$2{I}_{0}$

For second case:

${I}_{2} = 4{I}_{0}\cos^{2}\left(\dfrac{2\pi}{λ} \times \dfrac{λ}{3}\right) =$4{I}_{0}\cos^{2}\left(\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right) = {I}_{0}

Therefore, required value of\dfrac{{I}_{1} + {I}_{2}}{I0} =$3$.

$

questions.q: In a Young's double slit experiment, a laser light of $560$ nm produces an interference pattern with consecutive bright fringes' separation of $7 . 2mm$. Now another light is used to produce an interference pattern with consecutive bright fringes' separation of $8 . 1mm$. The wavelength of second light is _____~$nm .$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given here:& ${λ}_{1} = 560 \times {10}^{- 9}m$,~${β}_{1} = 7 . 2 \times {10}^{- 3}m$~and~${β}_{2} = 8 . 1 \times {10}^{- 3}m$.

Let $d$ be the width and $D$ be the distance between slit and screen then fringe width,~$\beta = \dfrac{\lambdaD}{d}$.

Thus, from above, $\beta ∝ \lambda$

So, the wavelength of second light is~${λ}_{2} = \dfrac{\beta2}{\beta1}{λ}_{1} = \dfrac{9}{8}{λ}_{1}$

$∴ {λ}_{2} = \dfrac{9}{8} \times 560 = 630nm .$

questions.q: The width of one of the two slits in a Young's double slit experiment is three times the other slit. If the amplitude of the light coming from a slit is proportional to the slit-width, the ratio of minimum to maximum intensity in the interference pattern is $x: 4$~where $x$ is~_______ .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given amplitude $\propto$ slit width
Also intensity $\propto(\text { Amplitude })^2 \propto(\text { Slit width })^2$
$\frac{I_1}{I_2}=\left(\frac{3}{1}\right)^2=9 \Rightarrow I_1=9 I_2$
$\frac{I_{\min }}{I_{\max }}=\left(\frac{\sqrt{I_1}-\sqrt{I_2}}{\sqrt{I_1}+\sqrt{I_2}}\right)^2=\left(\frac{3-1}{3+1}\right)^2=\frac{1}{4}=\frac{x}{4}$
$\Rightarrow x=1$

questions.q: In a Young's double slit experiment, the intensity at a point is \left(\frac{1}{4}\right)^{\text {th }}$ of the maximum intensity, the minimum distance of the point from the central maximum is ________ $\mu \mathrm{m}$. (Given : $\lambda=600 \mathrm{~nm}, \mathrm{~d}=1.0 \mathrm{~mm}, \mathrm{D}=1.0 \mathrm{~m}$ )$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{I}=\mathrm{I}_0 \cos ^2\left(\frac{\Delta \phi}{2}\right) \\ & \frac{\mathrm{I}_0}{4}=\cos ^2\left(\frac{\Delta \phi}{2}\right) \\ & \Delta \phi=\frac{2 \pi}{3} \\ & \frac{2 \pi}{\lambda}\left(\frac{\mathrm{yd}}{\mathrm{D}}\right)=\frac{2 \pi}{3} \\ & \mathrm{y}=\frac{\lambda \mathrm{D}}{3 \mathrm{~d}}=\frac{600 \times 10^{-9} \times 1}{3 \times 10^{-3}}=2 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{~m}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A double slit interference experiment performed with a light of wavelength 600 nm forms an interference fringe pattern on a screen with 10 th bright fringe having its centre at a distance of 10 mm from the central maximum. Distance of the centre of the same 10th bright fringe from the central maximum when the source of light is replaced by another source of wavelength 660 nm would be _________ mm .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Position of the $n^{\text {th }}$ bright fringe w.r.t. central maxima
in a YDSE is $y_n=n \frac{\lambda D}{d}$.
$\Rightarrow \quad \frac{y_{10}^{\prime}}{y_{10}}=\frac{\lambda^{\prime}}{\lambda}$
or $\quad y_{10}^{\prime}=\frac{\lambda^{\prime}}{\lambda} y_{10}$\begin{aligned} & =\left(\frac{660 \mathrm{~nm}}{600 \mathrm{~nm}}\right) 10 \mathrm{~mm} \\ & =11 \mathrm{~mm}\end{aligned}$$

questions.q: A fringe width of $6$ mm was produced for two slits separated by $1$ mm apart. The screen is placed $10m$ away. The wavelength of light used is $x$~$nm$. The value of $x$& to the nearest integer is ______.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\beta = \dfrac{\lambdaD}{d}$

$\lambda = \dfrac{\betad}{D}$

$\lambda = \dfrac{6 \times {10}^{- 3} \times {10}^{- 3}}{10}$

$\lambda = 6 \times {10}^{- 7}m = 600 \times {10}^{- 9}m$

$\lambda = 600nm$

questions.q: In Young's double slit experiment the two slits are $0 . 6mm$ distance apart. Interference pattern is observed on a screen at a distance $80$ cm from the slits. The first dark fringe is observed on the screen directly opposite to one of the slits. The wavelength of light will be _____~$nm$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
According to the question, the first dark fringe is observed directly opposite to one of the slits. Therefore, half of the fringe width is equal to& half of the distance between the slits.

$\dfrac{β}{2} = \dfrac{d}{2} ⇒ \beta = d = 6mm$

$⇒ \dfrac{\lambdaD}{d} = 0 . 6 \times {10}^{- 3} ⇒ \lambda = \dfrac{0 . 6 \times {10}^{- 3}d}{D} ⇒ \lambda = \dfrac{0 . 6 \times {10}^{- 3} \times 0 . 6 \times {10}^{- 3}}{80 \times {10}^{- 2}}$

$⇒ \lambda = 450 \times {10}^{- 9}m = 450nm$
